file: "Study of body floatation as a function of salinity".jpg
description:
Picture of an educational activity with the students in the scientific laboratory of the Middle School “Scuola Secondaria di Primo grado ‘Enrico Fermi’ in Castelplanio (An), Italy.
“Study of body floatation as a function of salinity”
The first glass container consists of water from the Adriatic Sea (3.5% of dissolved salt).
For the second glass container, the students recreated in the laboratory the conditions of the Dead Sea water. In order to be able to dissolve the significant amount of salt required (33.7%), the solution was heated up and subsequently cooled down.
The floatation was tested with the use of fresh eggs.
Teachers:
1. Daniele Sabbatini
2. Paolo Pigliapochi

3. Patrizia Scuppa

description:
Native American farmer and retired teacher Jerri Parker grew up on in agriculture, but now she operates her diversified farm in Cromwell, Oklahoma.
With hoop houses, vegetables, 300 chickens, eggs and beef, she started sell to the public in 2004. 
Here, Parker candles an egg to check for cracks and other deficiencies in the egg that would cause it to be rejected.

USDA photo by Preston Keres.

file: US, Ghana veterinarians provide animal healthcare at African Lion 2025 (9054241).jpg
artist: U.S. Army photo by 1st Lt. Katherine Sibilla
description:
U.S. Army Capt. Kylie Smith, a veterinarian assigned to Public Health Command Europe, inspects a chicken afflicted with lice during the medical readiness exercise (MEDREX) along with members of the Ghana Armed Forces Veterinary Services in Accra, Ghana, May 20, 2025. During the MEDREX, Smith had the opportunity to work with animals she had not treated before. Part of African Lion 2025 (AL25), this MEDREX is planned and executed by U.S. Army Southern European Task Force, Africa (SETAF-AF), and prepares U.S. military health professionals for the challenges of providing care outside of traditional clinical settings. By working alongside African partners, U.S. medical professionals refine their ability to deliver rapid, adaptable, and resource efficient medical care, directly increasing medical readiness for large scale combat operations. 
AL25, the largest annual military exercise in Africa, will take place from April 14 to May 23, 2025. Led by SETAF-AF, on behalf of U.S. Africa Command with over 10,000 troops from more than 50 nations, including seven NATO allies, across Ghana, Morocco, Senegal, and Tunisia. The exercise aims to bolster military readiness, enhance lethality, and foster stronger partnerships, ultimately improving joint capabilities in complex multi-domain environments to enable participating forces to deploy, fight, and win. (U.S. Army photo by 1st Lt. Katherine Sibilla)
